original_question: Which mathematically consistent fractional-calculus models should be used to formulate quantum mechanics with nonlocality in space and quantum field theory with nonlocality in space-time by passing from lattices with long-range interactions to their continuum limits?
target_in_paper: Section 4.3, final unnumbered sentence, read together with the setup in Section 4.1: the paper identifies as an important future direction the development of quantum mechanics with nonlocality in space and quantum field theory with nonlocality in space-time from lattice models with long-range interactions and their continuum limits.
correct_elements: The draft already captures the correct application area (quantum mechanics and quantum field theory), the correct kinds of nonlocality (space and space-time), and the specific lattice-to-continuum mechanism emphasized in the paper: models of lattices with long-range interactions and their continuum limits. Your added emphasis on mathematical consistency is also well motivated by the nearby discussion of exact fractional differences and the missing fundamental theorems of fractional calculus for non-integer orders.
missing_details: The paper does not ask readers to choose among already established models; it frames this as a future research direction to develop such formulations.
The intended framework is not arbitrary fractional quantum modeling, but the lattice-fractional-calculus / exact-differences approach arising from lattices with long-range interactions.
The discrete-to-continuum passage is part of the target itself: the continuum limit is described by fractional differential equations.
The main nearby mathematical caveat is explicit: for exact fractional differences of non-integer order, the fundamental theorems of fractional calculus have not yet been proved.

The target should be kept distinct from the time-nonlocal/non-Markovian open-quantum-system questions discussed earlier in Section 4.3, and also from the time-fractional Schrödinger-equation direction mentioned there only by contrast.

Section 4 frames the issue more generally as matching types of nonlocality with appropriate operator kernels, so a paper-faithful rewrite should mention fractional-calculus formulations rather than only unspecified 'models'.

Ambient ring/field, variable lists, homogeneity, degree restrictions, nilpotency conditions, quantifiers such as 'for all sufficiently large m', and similar algebraic data are not part of this paper's target statement and are inapplicable here, because the relevant target is an unnumbered research direction in mathematical physics rather than an algebraic conjecture or theorem.
refined_question: How can one construct a mathematically consistent fractional-calculus formulation of (i) quantum mechanics with nonlocality in space and (ii) quantum field theory with nonlocality in space-time by starting from lattice models with long-range interactions and passing to continuum limits described by fractional differential equations, specifically in the lattice-fractional-calculus / exact-fractional-differences framework where the fundamental theorems of fractional calculus for non-integer-order exact differences are still to be established?
justification: This paper does not contain a numbered conjecture or open problem matching the draft. The nearest official target is the final sentence of Section 4.3, which explicitly names quantum mechanics with spatial nonlocality and quantum field theory with space-time nonlocality, built from lattices with long-range interactions and their continuum limits. Section 4.1 supplies the hidden technical scope needed to make that sentence stand alone: long-range interactions are the source of spatial nonlocality; the continuum limit is described by fractional differential equations; the relevant discrete framework is lattice FC with exact differences; and the nearby mathematical obstruction is that the fundamental theorems of FC are still unproved for exact fractional differences of non-integer order. Section 4 also frames the overall goal as identifying the kinds of operator kernels appropriate for given kinds of nonlocality, which supports retaining a narrow formulation focused on the lattice-to-continuum FC construction rather than broadening to all nonlocal quantum models.
